jordan: Quick signal — after merging the slot allocator change (PR #742) I'm seeing a new memcpy hotspot on the small-batch, low-latency path. nsys timelines show repeated kernel flips + memcpy tailing. attaching traces :eyes:

elaine: saw the same in perfetto — scheduler slot shift around token ~12 causes kernel rebinds and a memcpy chain. latency bump ~0.5-0.8ms/token on 1-batch runs.

sam: bisect narrowed it down to commit abcdef1234 -> 9c3b4d (allocator: prefer-fill-slot heuristic change). behavior change looks intentional but perf regressed.

mike: confirmed locally with a short nsys run. Before: kernels stick to fast_variant; After: we hit memcpy_kernel_v2 more often. flamegraphs attached. :zap:

perf-bot: automated nsys run finished: s3://redwood-perf/nsys/3792468012/after.qdrep

jordan: thanks. can someone paste a minimal repro command? I'll run an nvprof/perf pair.

elaine: repro command I used:
```
NSYS_CMD="nsys profile -t cuda,cudnn,nvtx -o /tmp/trace_after"
$NSYS_CMD -- python -m runtimeserver --model t5-small --seq_len 64 --batch 1 --warmup 10 --iter 50
```

sam: also capture perfetto (cpu+gpu) to see scheduler handoffs + thread wakeups. I saw context-switch spikes aligning with slot swaps.

mike: quick diff of flamegraphs shows an extra cudaMemcpyAsync chain inserted between kernel selections after the change — likely due to temporary buffer handoff when we move work between slots.

elaine: I tried the --force-old-allocator flag and latency returned to baseline on the same machine. So it's the new slot preference logic for tiny occupancy cases.

jordan: OK. suggestion: open a revert PR while we investigate and add tests. Sam, can you bisect to the exact line?

sam: narrowing now; looks like scheduler/slot_allocator.cpp around line ~217 where we flip slot_preference when occupancy_threshold is hit. The flip moves work to another slot which triggers extra memcpy to reconcile KV cache pointers.

ops-bot: created issue #1193: "slot-allocator: regression after prefer-fill-slot change causing memcpy hotspot" — traces and perf links attached.

jordan: proposed plan:
1) revert allocator behavioral change to restore baseline for next canary
2) add unit/integration test that asserts kernel affinity for batch=1 and seq<=64
3) add perf regression check to CI that runs the small-batch microbenchmark and fails on >10% tail latency regression

elaine: +1
mike: +1
sam: I'll draft the revert PR and attach repro scripts & nsys/perfetto commands.

jordan: thanks — after revert we'll run A/B traces and land a more targeted fix (probably preserve prefer-fill logic but avoid slot moves that force memcpy for cached KV pointers). I'll monitor canary after revert.
__notes: thread contains root message and replies in chronological order; messages are short and Slack-style.
